integrator_questions: With mass at 1.0 kg, does the controller need more kp to hold the bend response, or less kd to stop the signal lagging? Compare the gain margin with the 0.8 kg run.
Where does max_error occur now: on the oval's tightest bend or on the s-bend and slalom? If the peak is still at bend entry, the limit is lag-limited and mass alone will not fix it.
Does steering_oscillation rise or fall with the heavier robot, and does control_effort or line_loss_events change on the slalom?

intent: Single-variable test of mass on the best geometry so far (iteration 3, 69.18). Mass goes from 0.8 kg to 1.0 kg, and every other value stays at the iteration 3 baseline. The 0.6 kg result fell 14 points, so the next step is to see whether the trend reverses above 0.8 kg. Expected: max_error at or below about 0.060 m, oval progress above 0.23, and a score above 69.18.
learning: Mass is now the only untested single variable on the best design. 0.6 kg was clearly worse (55.45 vs 69.18), so the optimum is at or above 0.8 kg. If 1.0 kg beats 0.8 kg, the next test is 1.2 kg or a sensor-pitch change. If 1.0 kg is worse, mass 0.8 kg is the local optimum and the next test is wheel_radius, or sensor pitch in isolation.
rationale: Scores by iteration on the same base design: 60 mm row, 0.12 m track, 0.8 kg gave 65.96. Moving the row to 40 mm gave 52.25, and 80 mm gave 69.18, the best so far. Narrowing the track to 0.10 m gave 53.14, and widening it to 0.14 m gave 60.26, so 0.12 m is the best track tested. Mass 0.6 kg on the 80 mm baseline gave 55.45, which is 13.7 points below the 0.8 kg best. Oval progress fell from 0.229 to 0.148 and the s-bend and slalom also worsened. Lighter is therefore worse, and the optimum mass is probably at or above 0.8 kg. Max error stays at 0.060 to 0.065 m on every track in every run, just over the 0.06 m off-track limit, while RMS error is 0.02 to 0.03 m. The failure is a transient peak on bends, and body width cannot move the limit. Iteration 6 suggests that more inertia or more grip helps, so I will test heavier mass in isolation. I am changing only mass, from 0.8 to 1.0 kg, on the iteration 3 baseline (80 mm row, 12 mm sensors on a 12 mm pitch, 0.12 m track, 0.03 m wheels, 0.12 m body width, 0.18 m body length). Expected: progress on the oval and slalom rises above the iteration 3 values, max error approaches 0.060 m, and the score exceeds 69.18. The risk is that extra mass adds rolling and slip losses, which would show as lower oval progress and a score below 69.
